title: Frontend: oscillator chart (Stochastic, Force Index) beneath the price chart
description: User request: the oscillator(s) used by Screen 2 (docs/Analyse.md — Stochastic %K(5,3,3) and Force Index, 2-period EMA) must also appear as a chart in the UI, sourced from the backend (no client-side recomputation, same principle as frontend-chart-signal-overlay). Add a new chart pane — a separate synced panel beneath/alongside the price chart (the conventional oscillator-pane layout, since these values are on a different scale than price and don't belong on the same axis as candlesticks) — plotting the historical Stochastic %K and Force Index series from the api-stocks-indicator-history endpoint, with reference lines at the documented oversold/overbought thresholds (30/70 for Stochastic per docs/Analyse.md §4). If MACD Histogram (Screen 1's weekly slope input, also table-listed in §4) is also wanted as a plotted oscillator rather than just the point-in-time value already in IndicatorsPanel, include it here too — decide and record as a decisions entry. Additional chart panels beyond what's listed here may be added if needed for clarity (e.g. splitting Stochastic and Force Index into separate panes instead of one shared one) — record any such addition as a decisions entry explaining why.

checklist.step: Decide which oscillator(s) to plot (Stochastic %K required per the user's request; Force Index required; MACD Histogram optional) and the pane layout (one shared oscillator pane vs. multiple), recording as a decisions entry.
Wire a TanStack Query hook for the oscillator series (reuse the hook added by frontend-chart-signal-overlay for the same endpoint if it covers this data, rather than duplicating the fetch).

Implement the oscillator pane using Lightweight Charts (or another already-in-use charting approach — check PriceChart.tsx's library first, prefer consistency over introducing a second charting library) as a new component under features/stocks/components/, synced in time range/interval with PriceChart.
Add reference lines/shading for the documented oversold/overbought thresholds (docs/Analyse.md §4) so the chart is readable against the methodology, not just raw numbers.
Handle loading/error/empty states consistently with the rest of the page (reuse LoadingState/ErrorState/EmptyState).

Tests: component test(s) for the new oscillator chart, keeping the suite's no-live-network invariant (MSW-mocked); confirm 90% coverage gate still holds and Storybook still builds if any new common/ component was added.
